explanation: A = {x², 2x, 2, 0} is finite. For n ≥ 1, the nth derivative of ln(x) is (−1)^(n−1)(n−1)!x^(−n), giving infinitely many distinct functions. The nth derivative of √x is a nonzero constant times x^(1/2−n); its different exponents also give infinitely many distinct functions. Thus B and C only are infinite.
